The captured CO from the blast furnace gas is stripped and 2 conditioned into 99.99 vol% CO for transportation via a dedicated pipeline for sequestration off-site. 2 The quench tower overhead gas with enhanced vol% CO enters into the absorber for capturing the CO 2 2 through an exothermic reaction with a proprietary amine. Many research organizations and companies are developing and investigating carbon capture technologies to remove or reduce the quantity of CO from 2 gas. The increased CO levels in the atmosphere are primarily attributed to emissions from industrial 2 facilities and the combustion of fossil fuels for power generation. Solvent-based technologies, that interface with flue gas, are most common for post-combustion processes and represent the most promising technology for retrofitting existing power plants without carbon capture. ION’s proprietary advanced solvent is among the leading second-generation solvent systems currently, which is primarily developed for post-combustion low CO concentration sources. ION has consistently demonstrated significant reductions 2 in regeneration energy requirements compared to traditional aqueous mono-ethanolamine (MEA) throughout bench-scale and laboratory testing, small-scale pilot testing with coal, and large-scale pilot testing with natural gas-fired and residue fluid catalytic cracker flue gases. This reduction is directly correlated to ION’s physiochemical solvent characteristics, which include a higher carrying capacity, a lower specific heat capacity, and an advanced process design. ION chose to rapidly develop its technology by leveraging existing facilities with several global and local partners. Additionally, the performance metrics of emissions, solvent make-up rates, and material compatibilities can all be evaluated on systems baselined with MEA.
